topic.angle: A road network of more than 400,000 km

body.question: At the peak of Rome's development, the empire's roads added up to more than...
body.reveal: More than 400,000 km, of which over 80,500 km were stone-paved. 29 great military highways radiated from Rome, and 372 great roads linked the empire's 113 provinces. Builders laid rubble, gravel and stone in layers.

probes.question: How were Roman roads built?
options: Layers of rubble, gravel and stone

probes.question: True or false: all of the 400,000 km of Roman roads were stone-paved.

image_brief.show: File:Roman Appian Way.jpg shows a stone-paved section of the Appian Way (CC0, portrait)

claims.quote: The whole comprised more than 400,000 kilometres (250,000 miles ) of roads, of which over 80,500 kilometres (50,000 mi) were stone-paved

claims.claim: 29 great military highways radiated from Rome; 372 great roads linked 113 provinces

claims.quote: Into the fossa was placed large amounts of rubble , gravel and stone, whatever fill was available
